To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we discovered a novel PPAR agonist that binds to PPARα and to PPARγ with a different binding mode; 2) we solved the crystal structures of the ligand in the complex with both receptors; 3) the ligand induces a different activation of PPARα and of PPARγ, which can be explained by the ligand binding mode.
we have identified a novel PPAR ligand with a unique binding mode that can be used as a template for the development of more balanced PPAR modulators.
we discovered a novel PPAR ligand with a very attractive profile and that we identified a new pocket in PPARα, whose filling is allowed in a ligand-induced conformational change.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery and characterization of new PPAR agonists, which could represent valuable tools to improve the current therapeutic strategies for the treatment of the metabolic syndrome.

the identification and characterization of novel PPAR ligands, with the goal to find new molecules that are more effective than the current PPAR modulators in terms of efficacy, selectivity, safety and tolerability.
the discovery of a new ligand binding mode for PPARs that can be exploited to design novel PPAR partial or selective agonists with a better therapeutic index.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ligand is a pan-agonist, able to induce the same activity profile in all the three isoforms.
this novel ligand binding pocket in PPARα is a new target to be explored in the search for new PPARα partial agonists.
our approach allowed to identify the first ligand that binds to PPARα and to PPARγ in a novel binding mode, and to rationalize the different activity profile of the two isoforms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ligand-induced opening of a pocket in PPARα, not present in PPARγ, is responsible for the partial activation of PPARα.
the ligand-induced conformational switch of PPAR F273 is a key factor for the PPARα activation and that a novel ligand pocket is formed by the F273 side-chain opening.

the identification of a PPAR pan- agonist with a very balanced activity profile is possible and the structure of the PPARα complex with a ligand binding to a new pocket provides a rationale for its activity profile.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PPARα is more permissive than PPARγ towards the binding of ligands in new pockets, which could be exploited for the design of novel partial or full PPARα agonists.

the ligand-induced conformational changes in the PPARs, which have been previously observed in the PPARα and the PPARγ structures, are not limited to a specific receptor, but they are a general mechanism for PPAR activation.

PPARα and γ can be activated by ligands that do not fit the classical binding pocket and that the activation is determined by the ligand ability to fill a new pocket in PPARα and the classical pocket in PPARγ.
